answer: Latency-Gradient Gating (LGG): Each payout requires the agent to complete a randomized 60s challenge over its own network path, reporting round-trip samples to a public terrace of timestamped checkpoints; a hidden classifier scores sable (low-variance) vs pearl (high-variance) jitter signatures. Clones sharing NAT/VM time entropy are correlated and frozen. Cost: attacker must rent distinct live egress and hardware per clone, plus lose unclaimed rewards on detection—each marginal clone costs more than its expected payout.
